summary: This October 10, 2023 article examines how remote work has become a lasting part of the local economy and job market after the pandemic. It covers productivity, digital infrastructure, shifts in local spending, work-life balance, remote team culture, inclusivity, and environmental benefits, using quotes from local business people. It concludes that many companies are moving toward hybrid models and will keep adapting policies based on employee feedback.
one_line: A local-economy article on how remote work has become a permanent post-pandemic fixture, with its effects on productivity, spending, culture, inclusion and the environment.
key_facts: The article is dated October 10, 2023 and describes remote work as 'one of its main engines' of modern business rather than an accessory.

Sarah Blakely, head of a mid-sized marketing firm in the city, sent her employees home on March 15, 2023 for indefinite remote work and found her team sometimes surpassed previous in-office performance metrics.
John Grant, a local tech startup founder, said offering employees freedom to shape their workdays made creativity surge and accelerated the product development cycle.
Timothy Rivera, an IT manager at a leading e-commerce company, said on September 4, 2023 that his firm had doubled its investment in secure remote access tools.
High-speed internet has gone from luxury to an essential utility, and companies are investing heavily in cloud services, project management tools, and cybersecurity.
Remote work has shifted spending to local areas: coffee shops with robust Wi-Fi and co-working spaces are proliferating, and small businesses in less densely populated areas benefit.
Lauren Evans, who manages a popular suburban coffee shop, said her business thrives because remote workers stay for hours.
Mallory Keaton, a graphic designer working from home, praised the flexibility to attend her daughter's soccer games but finds it hard to stop working with her office in the next room.
Alex Jensen, People Operations Director at a local software firm, said virtual escape rooms and online trivia nights help maintain community among remote teams.
Samantha Wu, a remote recruiter, said hiring beyond city limits has enriched workforce diversity and brought fresh perspectives.
Remote work can open employment to people with disabilities, caretakers, and individuals in rural areas by removing geographic barriers.
Eco-consultant Derek Summers said companies going remote have 'unintentionally become environmental stewards' through lower emissions, energy use, and paper waste.
Some companies foresee a gradual return to the office, but many envision a hybrid model blending remote work with occasional in-person interactions.
